newsitem.title: GERMANY: German coffee consumers await lower prices.
newsitem.headline: German coffee consumers await lower prices.

text.p: German coffee roasters feel weak conditions in New York on Friday may bring further price reductions this week, traders said on Monday.
"Consumers need some more nearby coffee but shy away from May, which is still at a considerable premium," one said.
"They would like to see another 10 cents off before entering the market and they feel encouraged by better supply news," he added.
Traders also said business was calming down ahead of the Easter (March 28-31) holidays.
New York May arabicas ended Friday at 165.75 cents/lb and July at 155.55 cents, off 3.40 and 1.65 cents respectively.

Roasters, who had bought April shipments before prices came off the two-and-a-half year highs seen a little over a fortnight ago, noted the way differentials had now eased and would have offered them savings for next month.
Roasters implemented prices increases for roasted coffee ex-works by one mark per 0.5 kg on March 10 but had no intention of reversing that move, traders said.
"The retail price rises, which were modest compared to other European countries, are still working their way through the system," one said.
"There will be a fall in consumption after Easter, which roasting companies have to absorb, and the higher price will help them live through that period."
"Further ahead, we're entering the Brazil frost season when raw material buyers want to operate from a solid financial base to be prepared for weather rallies."
In the domestic market, Central American and Colombian origin offers were scarce but second hand sellers were able to trade some material at lower differentials.
Kenyans sold at high prices while higher internal Brazilian prices discouraged importers here.
Latin American arabica prices were $8-17 down on the week per 50 kg fob, with Brazils at $183, off $11.
Vietnam robustas were off $1.50 at $75.00 per 50 kg cif.
